correctness.rationale: For r=1−η in (0,1), an epoch composes to r²x±η², so the RR and IID second moments are geometric sums with the same numerator factor 1−r^(4m), giving η²/(1+r²) for every m≥1. The respective signed affine maps cover their invariant convex hulls exactly at contraction ≥1/2. Below that contraction the strict first-level separation proves the RR gap and the separated cylinders give the stated dimension. The worst cancellation of all but the leading RR sign realizes g+η²q^m/(1−q), so g is the limiting uniform forbidden radius. For q≥1/2 weak convergence and full invariant support rule out any uniform open hole at all finite epoch endpoints. At η=1/2 the finite IID sign histories biject with odd numerators over denominator 2^(2m); RR is IID conditional on opposite signs within each epoch (probability 2^(−m)), so TV is 1−2^(−m). The half-step stationary laws are singular by dimension 1/2 versus uniform Lebesgue density, not merely by lack of a shared neighborhood. At other comparison steps full IID support does not imply absolute continuity. Independent dyadic checks through eight epochs replay with `python /workspace/replay_frozen_reviews.py 5`; they do not establish the infinite-time claims.
